apportion.empty: No drives with usable coordinates in this window.
apportion.subtitle: Confidence is 95% when both endpoints fall in the same box, 70% when only one does, and 60% for a cross-border split.
apportion.title: Apportionment by jurisdiction

digest.body: A stable fingerprint of the apportionment above. If the underlying drives change, the digest changes — which is exactly what makes a sealed filing meaningful.
digest.title: Period digest

filings.subtitle: Sealing a period snapshots the distance, energy and charge behind a digest, so a later dispute can be settled against the exact figures you filed.
filings.title: Sealed filings

notice.body: Rates are the ones you enter; boundaries are simple bounding boxes. A drive that starts in one jurisdiction and ends in another is split evenly and flagged at reduced confidence. Use this to prepare and cross-check a filing — never as the filing itself.
notice.title: A worksheet, not a tax return

rates.subtitle: When boxes overlap, the smallest one that contains the point wins — so a city can sit inside a state.
rates.title: Jurisdiction rate table

compliance.subtitle: Apportion every metre you drove to the jurisdiction it happened in, price it against that jurisdiction’s road-usage rate, and seal the period into an immutable filing record.
compliance.title: Jurisdictional Compliance & Road-Usage Charge

unsupported.polygon: True polygon boundaries — jurisdictions are approximated by bounding boxes
unsupported.submit: Submitting to a tax authority, and any legal interpretation of what is owed

form.label: Part label
form.ratedDaysHint: Filters and fluids age on the calendar too

lifecycles.empty: Record a part below and its lifecycle projection appears here.
lifecycles.title: Part-by-part projection

notice.body: The wear multiplier is derived from your own drives, clamped to a defensible range. It is a projection, not a measurement of physical wear — always inspect before relying on it for a safety-critical part.
notice.title: Duty cycle beats the manual

stress.empty: Not enough drives yet to characterise your duty cycle.
stress.label: Duty-cycle factor
stress.subtitle: Each factor compares a measured trait of your driving against a reference profile. Multipliers compound, then clamp.
stress.title: Why your wear rate differs

consumables.subtitle: Rated life assumes an average car. Yours is not average — this projects each part against your measured speed profile, regen share, power draw and climate, then tells you which limit will actually retire it.
consumables.title: Consumables & Wear-Parts Lifecycle

unsupported.physical: Measuring physical wear — no tread-depth or pad-thickness sensor exists on the vehicle
unsupported.recall: Manufacturer service bulletins and recalls affecting a part

chart.aria: Bar chart of drive share and aggression score per behaviour cluster
chart.empty: Not enough drives in this window to separate behaviour clusters.
chart.title: Cluster mix and driving intensity

clusters.subtitle: Cohesion is the mean feature distance inside the cluster — lower is tighter.
clusters.title: Cluster characteristics

fingerprints.empty: No drives with sufficient telemetry in this window.
fingerprints.subtitle: Every drive scored against each cluster centroid. Labelling one drive re-anchors the whole cluster.
fingerprints.title: Drive fingerprints

notice.body: Clusters are derived only from drive dynamics already stored on this server. No cameras, no seat sensors, no accounts. A cluster stays anonymous until you choose to name it.
notice.title: Behavioural, never biometric

profiles.subtitle: Name a cluster once by labelling any drive it contains; the whole cluster inherits the name.
profiles.title: Named drivers

stat.ambiguousHint: Two clusters fit almost equally well

driver.subtitle: Group drives by how they were driven — speed discipline, power draw, regen use and departure hour — then attach a name once and let every future drive inherit it.
driver.title: Driver Fingerprinting & Attribution

unsupported.identity: Proving who was physically in the seat — this infers behaviour, not identity
unsupported.passengers: Distinguishing a driver who deliberately changes style from a second driver

verdict.moderate: Clusters overlap somewhat. Label a few more drives per cluster to sharpen the boundary.
verdict.strong: Clusters are well separated — attributions can be trusted for cost splitting.
verdict.title: Interpretation
verdict.weak: Behaviour is too similar to separate reliably. Treat attributions as indicative only.

error.body: Review the inputs and try again.
error.title: Request could not be completed

evidence.subtitle: Measured observations are separated from modelled assumptions and from fields the engine will not compute.
evidence.title: Evidence, quality, and limitations

form.downsampleHint: Leave blank to keep full resolution

impact.empty: Run the dry-run plan above to see what a policy would reclaim.
impact.subtitle: Fidelity loss is the share of analytical resolution the plan would remove — not the share of rows.
impact.title: Dry-run impact

inventory.subtitle: Live sizes read from the database catalog. Toggle datasets to scope the dry run.
inventory.title: Dataset inventory

notice.body: Every run on this page is a read-only dry run. TeslaSync computes what a policy would remove and records the plan in the ledger; it never issues a delete. Enforcement remains a deliberate, separate operator action outside this screen.
notice.title: Plan only — nothing is ever deleted here

policies.subtitle: A policy declares intent. It becomes a plan only when you run the simulation.
policies.title: Retention policies

runs.subtitle: An append-only history of every plan computed, so retention decisions are auditable after the fact.
runs.title: Plan ledger

governance.subtitle: See exactly what every table costs you on disk, model a retention policy, and quantify the analytical fidelity you would trade away — before anything is deleted.
governance.title: Data Retention & Lifecycle Governance

unsupported.delete: Actually deleting rows — this screen is deliberately read-only
unsupported.index: Index and TOAST overhead attribution below table granularity

factors.empty: No factor had enough samples to score in this window.
factors.subtitle: Every weighted signal behind the score, with the baseline it was measured against.
factors.title: Factor decomposition

form.subtitle: Money is entered in ISO-4217 minor units so no cent is lost to floating point.
form.title: Policy baseline

levers.empty: No lever produced a material saving at the current score.
levers.subtitle: What each behavioural change is worth, ordered by payoff per unit of effort.
levers.title: Ranked improvement levers

notice.body: The premium simulation applies your policy’s own stated maximum telematics discount to a loss-cost index derived from measured exposure. It is an internal negotiation aid, never an insurer quote.
notice.title: Modelled, not quoted

packet.empty: A packet hash is produced once a profile has been computed.
packet.subtitle: A stable content hash over the exposure, factors, and window. Quote it when disputing a rating so both sides know they are looking at the same dataset.
packet.title: Insurer evidence packet

premium.empty: Register a policy below to simulate a telematics-adjusted premium.
premium.subtitle: What the stored policy would cost if the telematics discount tracked the measured loss cost.
premium.title: Premium simulation

insurance.subtitle: Actuarial frequency × severity underwriting built from your own measured driving, with a premium simulation and ranked improvement levers.

summary.empty: Select a vehicle to build an underwriting profile.
summary.subtitle: Exposure-normalised risk over the selected window.
summary.title: Underwriting position

insurance.title: Insurance Telematics Studio

trend.chartAria: Area chart of rolling insurance risk score over the analysis window
trend.empty: At least two buckets of driving are needed to plot a trajectory.
trend.subtitle: Rolling risk score and loss cost across the window — a rising line means underwriting exposure is growing.
trend.title: Risk trajectory

unsupported.claims: Actual claim history — the model uses driving exposure only
unsupported.quote: Binding quotes, carrier acceptance, or regulatory rate approval

quality.title: Data quality
quality.unavailable: Quality metadata has not been computed yet.

audit.empty: Select a statement above to run the audit.
audit.subtitle: Net variance is what the provider owes you (positive) or what you under-paid (negative).
audit.title: Reconciliation result

buckets.empty: No material variance was attributed on this statement.
buckets.subtitle: Every currency unit of disagreement is assigned a cause, so a dispute never rests on "the number looks wrong".
buckets.title: Variance attribution

dispute.empty: Audit a statement before opening a dispute.
dispute.none: No disputes recorded on this statement.
dispute.subtitle: The packet digest fixes exactly which lines and measurements your claim rests on.
dispute.title: Dispute desk

invoices.empty: No statements imported yet for this vehicle.
invoices.subtitle: Import a statement, then pick one to audit line by line.
invoices.title: Provider statements

lines.empty: This statement has no lines to reconcile.
lines.title: Line-by-line audit

notice.body: Lines are matched on start time and delivered energy, then scored. A line only becomes disputable when the measured session disagrees beyond tolerance — never merely because it was unmatched.
notice.title: Your telemetry is the reference

reconcile.subtitle: Match every billed line against the session your car actually recorded, attribute the variance to a cause, and assemble a dispute packet you can send to the provider.
reconcile.title: Charging Invoice Reconciliation

uninvoiced.empty: Every measured session in this period appears on the statement.
uninvoiced.subtitle: Measured sessions inside the billing period with no matching line. Usually free or home charging — occasionally a statement that is genuinely incomplete.
uninvoiced.title: Sessions the provider never billed

unsupported.submit: Submitting the dispute to the provider — the packet is prepared, not sent
unsupported.tax: Tax and idle-fee legality, which vary by site contract

chart.aria: Bar chart of return on spend percentage for each subscription, coloured by verdict
chart.empty: No subscription has enough measured usage to compute a return yet.
chart.title: Return by subscription

form.benchmarkHint: What one unit of this usage would cost without the subscription
form.name: Name

list.empty: No subscriptions recorded for this vehicle.
list.name: Subscription
list.title: Subscription register

notice.body: Realised value is measured usage multiplied by the benchmark rate you set — what the same usage would have cost without the subscription. A subscription active for under 30 days is reported as too early to judge, never as a loss.
notice.title: Value is what you would otherwise pay

roi.empty: Record a subscription below to start measuring its return.
roi.subtitle: Confidence falls when the active period is short or the usage metric has sparse data — a low-confidence "cancel" is a prompt to look, not to act.
roi.title: Per-subscription verdict

subscription.subtitle: Price every recurring charge against the usage it actually delivered, express the break-even in units you can act on, and see exactly how much cancelling the weak ones would return.
subscription.title: Subscription & Feature ROI

unsupported.cancel: Cancelling a subscription with the provider — this measures, it does not transact
unsupported.intangible: Convenience and enjoyment, which have real value but no measurable unit here

bands.empty: Run a replay to break down band usage.
bands.none: This plan has a single undifferentiated rate.
bands.subtitle: Band occupancy for each plan — this is the mechanism behind the ranking, not a projection.
bands.title: Where your energy actually landed

chart.aria: Bar chart comparing annualised cost of each evaluated tariff plan
chart.caption: Annualised cost comparison
chart.empty: Run a replay to populate this chart.
chart.subtitle: Green is the cheapest ranked plan; grey bars are the alternatives you would be paying instead.
chart.title: Annualised cost by plan

controls.all: No plans selected — every stored plan will be evaluated.
controls.subtitle: Shiftable share is the fraction of energy you could realistically move into the cheapest band without changing when you drive.
controls.title: Comparison parameters

notice.body: Each plan is priced against the exact sessions you actually charged, bucketed into their real time-of-day bands. Annualisation scales the observed window — it does not predict future consumption.
notice.title: Replay, not forecast

plans.empty: No plans yet — add the plan you are on today plus any you are considering.
plans.subtitle: Author any plan your utility offers. Prices are stored per watt-hour in currency minor units so exotic structures stay exact.
plans.title: Your rate plan library

results.empty: No plan produced a priced result — check that your plans have at least one price band.
results.title: Ranked plan economics

tariff.subtitle: Replay your real measured charging load against every rate plan you can author — flat, time-of-use, tiered, real-time, and demand — then rank them on annualised cost.

summary.empty: Run a replay to see how much your plan choice is worth.
summary.title: Arbitrage summary

tariff.title: Utility Tariff Arbitrage Lab

unsupported.future: Future utility price changes, seasonal reindexing, or regulatory riders
unsupported.home: Household load outside the vehicle — only measured charging sessions are priced

calibration.chart: Mean absolute error and bias per bin
calibration.empty: Select a scorecard with enough scored samples to plot its calibration.
calibration.title: Calibration by prediction magnitude

cards.empty: No models have enough scored predictions yet in this window.
cards.subtitle: Drift ratio compares recent-half error against early-half error. Above 1.5 means the model is getting worse.
cards.title: Model scorecards

form.unitHint: Derived from the target so stored predictions stay SI-canonical.

notice.body: A prediction only counts once its outcome is recorded. Skill is measured against a naive persistence baseline, so a model that merely repeats the last value scores zero — not high.
notice.title: Scored against reality, not against itself

predictions.empty: No predictions recorded for this vehicle yet.
predictions.subtitle: Record a forecast before the fact, then score it once the outcome is known. Nothing here can be edited after the fact.
predictions.title: Prediction ledger

trust.subtitle: Every forecast this platform makes is written down, then scored against what actually happened. Bias, calibration, skill against a naive baseline, and drift over time decide whether a model earns your trust.
trust.title: Prediction Accuracy & Model Trust Lab

unsupported.cause: Explaining why a model drifted; it reports that it did
unsupported.retrain: Retraining or auto-correcting a model — this lab measures, it does not tune

bundle.body: A stable digest over the coverage terms and readiness state used for this assessment. Quote it when you open a claim so both sides reference the same snapshot.
bundle.title: Evidence bundle

claims.subtitle: Record what you asked for and what came back, so the next claim starts from a known history.
